items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: Kreutzmann came back and Billy Hart, he’s back, and they had to have Kreutzmann because Billy, he could play a lot of things but time is not one of them.

ctx.x: Oh well, you know, God, first of all Bob Weir is really a good friend of mine. And the way we met was through Michael Nash and Carrie Williams. They asked me to be part of this — of writing the music for a musical about Satchel Paige. And so we began to collaborate, Taj Mahal, Bob Weir and myself, Michael Nash and Carrie were writing the libretto. And it’s been a process now that’s been going on for seven years you know. And I think — we’ve had several workshops, we had Avery Brooks come in and direct us, we’ve…

Then he dies, right in the middle of his time, and it’s just incredible that, I mean I never got paid a dime to play with them but what I did get was all this recognition from all these people. Every time I played a concert, somebody would come in with a shirt like this and say, “Play one for Jerry, Dave.” You know, I’m like okay. And so then I did an album of their music. Because they were really such nice people. I was like well hey let me take your music and put it in a jazz thing, let’s put this together and…
That’s great. You seem to have the most wide open ears I can imagine. Even—
